title: Apple Launching Two More New Products This Friday - MacRumors
text:
Monday November 9, 2026 4:19 am PST by Tim Hardwick

The Apple launches keep coming! The company is set to release two new products on Friday, November 13: the all-new Apple HomeView and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, both of which have been available to pre-order since mid-October. 

- Apple HomeView: Apple's new smart home display, powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, for entertainment and managing the home. Available in tabletop and wall-mounted models, it can recognize up to six users by face, each with a personalized Home Screen. The HomeView is priced at $299.
- Apple TV 4K: adds Siri AI, the A19 chip, an updated Siri Remote with Find My, and support for four-speaker surround sound with HomePod mini 2. The Apple TV 4K comes with 128GB of storage and is priced at $299.

Both products were announced on October 13 alongside the HomePod mini 2, which launched October 30. 

As things stand, HomeView will not be sold in the European Union because Siri AI is currently unavailable on iOS in the region due to regulatory constraints. Apple has said it is "working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," but has provided no timeline for EU availability.

title: Apple 'Welcome Home' event — 9 things we learned and all the launches, from the Apple HomeView to a new Apple TV 4K | TechRadar
text:
# Apple 'Welcome Home' event — 9 things we learned and all the launches, from the Apple HomeView to a new Apple TV 4K

 By David Nield 

 Published 13 October 2026 

A host of new products

 Apple has new hardware to show off (Image credit: Apple) 

After treating us to the grand unveiling of the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo handsets in September, Apple returned in October to launch some notable device upgrades in the smart home and streaming categories.

There are refreshed versions of the Apple TV 4K and the HomePod mini, plus an Echo Show-style smart display called the HomeView. The HomeView is evidence of a renewed focus on the smart home from Apple, as are the devices being made by LG Electronics and Schneider Electric that the HomeView can connect to.

We've also got Siri AI rolling out across the board, which in theory should mean more intelligent and more useful AI conversations. Here's our full recap of what was announced, with links to specific articles if you want to read more.

## 1. The HomeView is Apple's first smart display — and it comes in two versions

It's like an Echo Show for Apple fans (Image credit: Apple)

Apple just jumped into smart displays: the HomeView is a competitor to the Amazon Echo Show and the Google Nest Hub, giving you a 7-inch screen that lets you control smart home devices, chat to Siri AI, play music, and much more. You can choose between a HomeView on its own rotating stand, or a HomeView designed to be wall-mounted.

A curated list of Apple apps can run on the HomeView, including Calendar, Safari, FaceTime, Weather, and Apple TV. If you like what you see, the HomeView costs $299 / £299 / AU$449 in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, or Space Gray. Preorders are open today, with sales and shipping starting on Friday, November 13.

...

## 3. The Apple TV 4K has finally been refreshed (with a big price hike)

A new Apple TV 4K for 2026, any takers? (Image credit: Apple TV 4K (2026))

We're pleased to see the launch of a brand new Apple TV 4K, but less enthused about the increased price: the new model will set you back $299 / £299 / AU$449, up from $199 / £199 / AU$299 (Wi-Fi) and $249 / £249 / AU$399 (Wi-Fi and Ethernet) for the old models, which are no longer going to be on sale from Apple.

You do get more for your money though. The upgrades here include a new Siri Remote that can make a sound when you're trying to find it, Siri AI on board, a faster processor, and three far-field mics for more "hey Siri" voice control options. Preorders are opening today, with a shipping and on-sale date of Friday, November 13.

title: Apple Has Another Product Launch on November 13 | The Apple Post
text:
Apple’s November product launches do not end with the five Macs and iPads arriving on November 6.

Exactly one week later, on Friday, November 13, Apple will launch two more products: the $299 HomeView smart home hub and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K.

The second launch day shifts Apple’s focus away from Mac and iPad and firmly into the living room and smart home.

## Apple HomeView arrives November 13

HomeView is Apple’s new shared smart home display, combining a 7-inch Liquid Retina screen with Siri AI, FaceTime, Apple Home controls, entertainment, and personalized experiences for different members of a household.

The tabletop HomeView and wall-mounted version both start at $299 in the United States, while the standard model costs £299 in the United Kingdom. The Apple Post has a full guide to everything HomeView can do.

...

The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K also goes on sale November 13, priced at $299 in the U.S. and £299 in the UK.

It introduces the A19 chip, three far-field microphones for hands-free Siri, Siri AI, a new Siri Remote with Precision Finding, and support for a four-speaker surround sound setup using compatible HomePod models. Here is everything you need to know about the new Apple TV 4K.

Both HomeView and Apple TV 4K have been available to pre-order since October 13, although some delivery estimates began slipping beyond launch day shortly after pre-orders opened.

Apple confirms both products officially become available on Friday, November 13. Apple’s HomeView announcement and Apple TV 4K announcement detail the launch timing.

title: Apple Isn't Done With 2026: Here's What's Still Coming - MacRumors
text:
Apple's busiest season isn't over yet. Far from it. With hardware launch dates still to come in November, plus software updates, streaming events, and new smart home accessories running into December, there's more on the way from Apple before the end of 2026, so be sure to stick around.

 Below, we've rounded up what's still coming, along with one date in particular that's worth watching if you're a holiday shopper. 

- Five new products – November 6: Apple is launching five products today: the OLED iPad mini with A20 Pro (from $699), the M6 iMac (from $1,499), the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 (from $1,999), and all-new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with OLED touchscreens (from $2,899 and $3,399). The latter two are Apple's first touchscreen Macs. Individual delivery dates vary based on region and configuration.
- Apple Creator Studio updates – rolling out November: Apple began rolling out the Creator Studio updates today, starting with Logic Pro, with more apps in the suite to follow throughout November. The updates bring built-in MotionVFX content to Final Cut Pro, Generate Fill to Pixelmator Pro, and new AI assistants in beta to Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. They are free for existing subscribers.
- Apple HomeView – November 13: Apple's new smart home display arrives on Friday, November 13, priced at $299. Available in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, the hub can be used to answer questions with Siri AI, display pictures, make FaceTime calls, play music, show recipes, offer up calendar events, and more. Pre-orders are already open in launch markets, but HomeView will not initially be sold in the European Union.
- Apple TV 4K – November 13: The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K launches alongside HomeView, and is also priced at $299. Unlike previous generations, there's just the one model with 128GB storage, and it adds Siri AI and supports four-speaker surround sound with HomePod mini 2 or second-generation HomePod speakers. Pre-orders are already open.
- Black Friday – November 27: It's not a product launch, but a date likely worth marking. Apple has held a four-day shopping event over the Black Friday weekend in recent years, when it has typically offered gift cards with eligible purchases. Our Black Friday roundup will be tracking the deals.
- App Store Awards – expected November and December: Dates for this year's awards are expected to follow last year's pattern, when Apple named its finalists on November 19 and announced the winners on December 4. The same schedule would put the 2026 finalists in late November and the winners in early December.
- Apple Music Replay – expected December: The full 2026 Replay recap is expected around the same time as last year's, when the full version became available on December 2, with your top songs, artists, and listening stats for the year.
- iOS 27.3 – December: Apple says iOS 27.3 will be released to the public in December, though it hasn't given a date. The first iOS 27.3 beta arrived on Tuesday, November 3. Beta features can change before release, but so far it includes new Siri AI actions across apps, vertical Tabs and an Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari, the redesigned Health app, a new Apple Fitness+ Gym Strength workout that builds a four-week plan, and more. Our iOS 27.3 beta guide has the full list.
- Apple Intelligence in China – December: The first Apple Intelligence features for users in China are already in testing in the iOS 27.3 beta, and Apple has confirmed the public rollout for December alongside the update. Apple has partnered with Alibaba to add Qwen support to Siri, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence. The initial release is for supported iPhones, with other platforms to follow after the required regulatory approvals, and it does not include Siri AI.
- Apple Home Collection – from December: The new Apple-backed, third-party lineup includes smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Apple says that availability begins in December, although select accessories will not arrive until early 2027.

title: Apple October 13 Event Time Around the World | The Apple Post
text:
# Apple ‘Welcome home’ event time: When it starts in your country

 David Joseppi Posted On 13/10/2026 

Apple’s “Welcome home” product launch takes place on Tuesday, October 13, with the company’s New York media experience beginning at 9 a.m. Eastern Time.

That time is confirmed for the in-person Apple Experience in Tribeca, but there is an important distinction for anyone planning to follow the announcements online: Apple has not said exactly how the new products will be revealed, or whether a public presentation will begin at the same time.

Apple marketing chief Greg Joswiak teased the October 13 launch with the “Welcome home” message, while invited journalists and creators have been told to arrive in New York for 9 a.m. ET.

## Apple October 13 event time around the world

The 9 a.m. ET start for Apple’s New York media experience works out to the following times around the world:

- United States and Canada: 6 a.m. PDT in Los Angeles and Vancouver; 7 a.m. MDT in Denver; 8 a.m. CDT in Chicago; 9 a.m. EDT in New York and Toronto; 10 a.m. ADT in Halifax; 10:30 a.m. NDT in St. John’s.
- Mexico: 7 a.m. in Mexico City.
- Brazil and Argentina: 10 a.m. in São Paulo and Buenos Aires.
- United Kingdom and Ireland: 2 p.m.
- Portugal: 2 p.m.
- France, Germany, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Central Europe: 3 p.m.
- Finland, Greece and Romania: 4 p.m.
- Turkey and Saudi Arabia: 4 p.m.
- South Africa: 3 p.m.
- United Arab Emirates: 5 p.m.
- Pakistan: 6 p.m.
- India: 6:30 p.m.
- Bangladesh: 7 p.m.
- China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Taiwan and the Philippines: 9 p.m.
- Japan and South Korea: 10 p.m.
- Indonesia: 8 p.m. in Jakarta and 9 p.m. in Bali.
- Australia: 9 p.m. in Perth; 10:30 p.m. in Darwin; 11 p.m. in Brisbane; 11:30 p.m. in Adelaide; midnight on October 14 in Sydney, Melbourne and Hobart.
- New Zealand: 2 a.m. on October 14 in Auckland and Wellington.

## We still do not know how Apple will reveal the products

Unlike a typical Apple keynote, the company has not confirmed a livestream or a full prerecorded presentation for October 13. The launch is also being described as an Apple Experience rather than a conventional Apple Event.

That leaves several possibilities. Apple could publish a series of Newsroom announcements, release shorter product videos, unveil the products privately in New York before making them public online, or combine several of those approaches.

The 9 a.m. ET time should therefore be treated as the confirmed start of the New York experience, not a guarantee that viewers around the world will see a keynote or product reveal begin at exactly that moment.

Apple is expected to focus on new smart home hardware, with The Apple Post’s full preview pointing to HomeView, a second-generation HomePod mini and a new Apple TV 4K as the headline products.

The new HomeView smart home hub is expected to be the centerpiece of the launch, with recent reports suggesting Apple will use the HomeView name for the display-equipped device.
